disclaimer: This explains your report in plain words. It is not a diagnosis and not medical advice. Only your doctor can tell you what these results mean for you.

note.what: TSH is the hormone your pituitary gland uses to tell your thyroid how much thyroid hormone to make; this test measures it.
note.ask: Do my TSH results point to a thyroid problem, and which other thyroid tests do you recommend?
note.source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine (US) — https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/tsh-thyroid-stimulating-hormone-test/ (updated 30 October 2024)
note.means: A higher TSH often suggests an underactive thyroid, meaning the thyroid is not making enough hormone; rarely it reflects a pituitary problem.

note.what: Free T4 measures the active, unbound form of thyroxine, the main hormone the thyroid makes, that enters your body tissues.
note.ask: What do my free T4 and TSH results mean together, and could any of my medicines or supplements be affecting them?
note.source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine (US) — https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/thyroxine-t4-test/ (updated 12 December 2024)
note.means: A lower result can be a sign of an underactive thyroid, and is also seen after treatment for an overactive thyroid or thyroid cancer.

summary: Your thyroid hormone levels suggest your thyroid may not be making enough hormone to keep your body working as it should. Please take this report to your doctor so they can examine you and decide what to do next.
